title: Peleg
summary: Son of Eber; "in his days was the earth divided" (Gen 10:25).

sorting_basis.note: Tier 1: CFAH anchor point: 2247 BC (AP-28, birth of Peleg)

birth.date: 2247 BC (birth of Peleg = final territorial division)
birth.citation: Griffith & White, "Chronological Framework of Ancient History. 4: Dating Creation and the Deluge," ARJ 16 (2023): 475–489, section "AP-28: Second/Final Territorial Division: 2247 B.C."
birth.note: AP-28: "from the birth of Peleg in 2247 BC (Ussher 2005, 21, §47)".

birth.citation: Jones, Chronology of the Old Testament (15th ed., 2002), "Chronological Compendium", p. 1 ("Peleg born when Eber was 34 ... 1757")
Ussher, Annals of the World, Second Age §47 (paragraph numbering of the modern transcription)

birth.date: Birth of Peleg: Anno Mundi 1757; 2173 B.C. (SBC)
birth.citation: Jordan, "Egypt in Biblical History," Biblical Chronology 5:8 (December 1993), second chart in section "The Beginnings of Egypt"
birth.note: Also BC 6:4 §7-8: "Peleg was born in am 1757 and lived 239 years, to the year 1996." B.C. year is Jordan's "SBC" (strictest Biblical chronology), which takes Daniel's 70 weeks literally from Cyrus (456 B.C. instead of the conventional 536 B.C.); not comparable one-to-one with Ussher/CFAH B.C. years.

birth.citation: Anno Mundi Chronology Studies (unnamed compiler; a compilation of James B. Jordan's system), p. 2, chart "Genesis 11:10 – 12 Genealogy"
birth.note: Agrees with Jordan's own published AM 1757.

birth.citation: Raleigh, The History of the World (1617, EEBO-TCP A10357), Chronological Table, sig. 782a
birth.note: Year cell "2440 1758 101". The third printed figure 101 is the column "Floud", not a length. To the Reader (sig. 780b): the Julian Period exceeds the yeere of the World by 682. The cell prints "1." and the name, and no length. Book I, sig. 113a says the division "was( if the diuision were made at Phalegs birth) in the yeere of the World 1757. or 1758." The table cell entered is the row at World 1758. 1757 is not entered as a second year.

birth.date: the division of the earth must be placed A. M. 1757, about one hundred and one years after the Flood, when Peleg the son of Eber was born
birth.citation: Shuckford, The Sacred and Profane History of the World Connected, 5th ed., revised by James Creighton (London: William Baynes, 1819), vol. 1, Book II, p. 94 (facsimile PDF p. 188)
birth.note: He says “if we suppose them to spend nineteen or twenty years in settling and building” before the confusion. Those nineteen or twenty years are not turned into a second Anno Mundi.

death.note: Not stated in the Jones sources read (Chart No. 1; Chronology of the Old Testament 15th ed. 2002, Chronological Compendium p. 1). Leave empty until verified.

death.citation: Ussher, Annals of the World, Second Age §60 (paragraph numbering of the modern transcription)

death.date: Death of Peleg: Anno Mundi 1996; 1934 B.C. (SBC)
death.citation: Jordan, "Egypt in Biblical History," Biblical Chronology 5:8 (December 1993), second chart in section "The Beginnings of Egypt"
death.note: B.C. year is Jordan's "SBC" (strictest Biblical chronology), which takes Daniel's 70 weeks literally from Cyrus (456 B.C. instead of the conventional 536 B.C.); not comparable one-to-one with Ussher/CFAH B.C. years.

death.citation: Anno Mundi Chronology Studies (unnamed compiler; a compilation of James B. Jordan's system), p. 2, chart "Genesis 11:10 – 12 Genealogy"
death.note: Agrees with Jordan's own published AM 1996.

death.date: The last yeere of Peleg his life.
death.citation: Raleigh, The History of the World (1617, EEBO-TCP A10357), Chronological Table, sig. 782b
death.note: Year cell "2678 1996 339". The third printed figure 339 is the column "Floud", not a length. To the Reader (sig. 780b): the Julian Period exceeds the yeere of the World by 682.
